trace.code: static bool pathToLogFile(LogFile& out, const std::string& path, int64_t size) {

preconditions: The victim (FoundationDB operator/analyst) runs fdbdecode --save (or fdbrestore) against a backup container the attacker controls or can inject files into (e.g. an S3/BlobStore bucket, a shared local directory, or a backup archive supplied for offline restore)
The backup container lists a range/log/snapshot file whose name contains one or more '..' path components before a valid file-name suffix (e.g. '../FDBWORMHOLE_PWNED/log,1,2,uid,1048576')
The running fdbdecode process has write permission at the traversal target (typically true for an operator restoring to their own machine)

evidence.fixed_version: main @ 414a6ec8 (merged 2026-10-26), backported to 7.4.10 (2026-11-16); NOT present in 8.0.0
evidence.observed_result: Vulnerable 8.0.0 pathToLogFile() validates only the last path component (fileNameOnly()) and stores the full attacker-controlled path in fileName, so fdbdecode --save's open(fileName, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) writes '../FDBWORMHOLE_PWNED/log,1,2,0123456789abcdef,1048576' OUTSIDE the output directory (<sandbox>/FDBWORMHOLE_PWNED/...). Fixed main rejects the same path via listedPathIsContained() -> relativePathIsContained() (rejects absolute paths and any '..' component). Marker: PATH TRAVERSAL CONFIRMED (vulnerable) / BLOCKED (fixed).

real_exploit.target: apple/foundationdb — the REAL pathToLogFile/pathToRangeFile/fileNameOnly from fdbclient/BackupContainerFileSystem.cpp @ 8.0.0 and the REAL relativePathIsContained/listedPathIsContained/pathToLogFile from main @ 414a6ec8, transcribed VERBATIM, plus the REAL DecodeProgress::openFile() save path from fdbbackup/FileDecoder.cpp @ 8.0.0 (only FDB logging/StringRef plumbing is stubbed)
real_exploit.backend: the verbatim vulnerable parser + the verbatim fdbdecode write path, driven against a real filesystem: an attacker-controlled '../ESCAPED/log,1,2,uid,1048576' name is accepted by the vulnerable pathToLogFile and the write lands outside the operator's output directory
real_exploit.demonstrated: A listed backup file name with a '..' component is accepted by the vulnerable pathToLogFile (8.0.0) and fdbdecode --save then performs platform::createDirectory() + open(O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) on that verbatim path, creating the file <sandbox>/FDBWORMHOLE_PWNED/log,1,2,0123456789abcdef,1048576 — OUTSIDE the intended output directory (arbitrary file write, CWE-22). The fixed parser rejects the identical name. A legitimate non-traversal name is still accepted by both, proving the fix does not over-block.

notes: 0-day in the current 8.x release line: the fix was merged to main on 2026-10-26 and backported to the 7.4 LTS line (7.4.10, tagged 2026-11-16), but 8.0.0 (tagged 2026-10-01) still contains the vulnerable code — verified by grepping 8.0.0's BackupContainerFileSystem.cpp (f.fileName = path with no listedPathIsContained check). Same CWE-22 pattern affects pathToRangeFile(), pathToKeyspaceSnapshotFile() (backup listing), fetchCheckpointFile() (checkpoint fetch), the profiler output path, and BulkLoad's assertLocalFolderContained(). Commit 414a6ec8 (PR #14347) follows cda9a9ec (PR #14341). Classified as CWE-22 (path traversal) -> arbitrary file write, a 'zip-slip'-style bug for FDB backups.
